newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba urges political leaders to fight corruption.
newsitem.headline: Cuba urges political leaders to fight corruption.

text.p: Cuban political leaders and managers at all levels must lead austere lifestyles and be on guard against corruption and abuse of office, Vice President Carlos Lage said.

Lage spoke at a ceremony on Tuesday evening to honour 54 officials and managers chosen for their good work and "faultless behaviour in the construction of socialism in our country," the ruling Communist Party newspaper Granma said on Wednesday.
Lage reiterated the key points of an ethics code for managers that was distributed around the country last year, which stresses that an efficient manager must also be personally austere.

Managers in Cuba were also political leaders, he said. They had to be "modest, austere, upright, deserving of the respect of the public", Lage said at the ceremony, which was presided over by President Fidel Castro.

"Each time a manager at any level loses energy to confront problems, falls into a routine, uses his job to live better, becomes too comfortable or becomes corrupt, this stains us all and it stains the Revolution," Lage said.
In recent years authorities have acknowledged that corruption exists in Cuba, speaking of the need to fight it.
State media last month reported that a former director of a state importing firm had been sentenced to 10 years in prison for corruption in his dealings with a foreign firm.

The growth of corruption appears to be linked to economic crises since the early 1990s, wider gaps between the rich and poor, and more contact with foreign businesses since the collapse of Cuba's old economic ally the Soviet Union.
